dominant_reason: R2a moved each preserved first tracking interval to a 30 s cleanStatic guard while retaining only the original nominal 1 ms sample residue, acquisition-grid carrier Doppler, and zero residual code/carrier phase. The receiver therefore started a nominal-rate local code at a future raw sample instead of restoring the code NCO and residual phase actually aligned to that sample. Carrier-aided code Doppler predicts 7.76 to 54.40 chips of unmodeled code drift across the eleven cleanStatic channels. The resulting nine-tap peak was at Prompt for only 9.02% of rows and at an outer tap for 35.70% of rows, while median carrier-lock tests collapsed from approximately 0.89-0.99 on ten supported R2 PRNs to approximately -0.01-0.08 in R2a.

cleanstatic_comparison.interpretation: The prompt-to-outer-tap displacement and lock collapse are the expected signature of starting the local C/A code at the wrong physical code phase; longer PLL/DLL warm-up cannot pull in a tens-of-chips initialization error with the frozen narrow nine-tap geometry.

bad_handoff_time_or_guard_selection.evidence: The 30 s guard is not intrinsically invalid, but relocating an old acquisition result to it without propagating receiver state creates the mismatch.

unstable_acquisition_to_tracking_state_i.evidence: The R2a handoff branch explicitly resets code NCO to 1023000 chips/s and both residual code phases to zero at the future target.

code_or_carrier_residual_convention_mism.evidence: The code epoch residue was copied but the code-Doppler-integrated phase was not. Absolute carrier accumulator was synthesized from grid Doppler rather than restored from the target-aligned receiver state.

doppler_or_frequency_initialization_mism.evidence: R2a retained the coarse acquisition-grid carrier Doppler. Those same grid values acquired and tracked ten cleanStatic PRNs in R2, so frequency alone does not explain the support collapse, but restoring the target-aligned filtered Doppler is safer.

pll_or_dll_warmup_transient.evidence: R2a produced about 15 s per channel after the 30 s guard yet never recovered stable lock on most PRNs. Filter and smoother warm-up should still be reset and audited after a physically aligned state restore.

prn_or_channel_subset_selection.evidence: The same fixed map contains ten PRNs with substantial R2 quality support; R2a collapsed nearly all of them simultaneously.

missing_receiver_internal_state_in_r2_sc.evidence: R2 schema v2 preserves target-aligned code/carrier NCO rates, residual code/carrier phases, filter outputs, accumulator, and interval length, but not full loop input histories or CN0/lock smoother histories. The repair will restore all preserved action state and deliberately re-warm unavailable histories without fabricating them.

true_receiver_limitation_requiring_fresh.evidence: The original R2 receiver tracks the same raw source and PRNs with strong support. Fresh instrumentation becomes required only if the preregistered target-aligned state restore still fails Phase A.
